subject: Optimize Toolkit: request for concession + batching/quantization ops plan (Parcelly)
content:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@parcelly.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Optimize Toolkit: request for concession + batching/quantization ops plan (Parcelly)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the detailed run rate data you shared last week. Attached is an updated illustration of the Optimize Toolkit credits + technical guardrails (OptKit_Tiered_Savings_v3.pdf) and a redline of the SOW for the pilot. High level: we can provide a 12% credit uplift in month 1 for a 6-month pilot, plus technical support for quantized runtime testing.

Before we lock terms, a few quick asks so we tailor the concession correctly:
- Can you confirm the steady-state RPS and the p50/p95 latency targets for your synchronous inference flows? (we saw spikes up to 1.8k RPS in the sample)
- Which endpoints will be latency-sensitive vs batchable (async) so we can map batching windows and prefix/KV cache coverage?
- Do you plan to test int8 quantization only, or would you like a faster OTE (optimize-to-empirical) path where our inference team runs quantization experiments for both int8 and int4 on your model snapshot?

I'll have Connor include a short ops-runbook and Kimberly will outline the credit drawdown schedule in the SOW. If you're good with the initial concession structure, we can push a DocuSign for signature and schedule a two-week kickoff for the runtime benchmarks.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OptKit_Tiered_Savings_v3.pdf] [Attachment: SOW_Parcelly_draft.docx]

---

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@parcelly.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: request for concession + batching/quantization ops plan (Parcelly)

Evelyn —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the revised SOW. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Traffic profile: steady-state ~650 RPS with daily peaks ~1.6k during promos. The most latency-sensitive route is /generate-chat (p95 target <= 400ms). Other endpoints (embeddings and rerank) can tolerate up to 2s and are good candidates for batching.

2) Quantization: we want Redwood to run the int8 experiments on our production model snapshot (we can share a sanitized copy via S3 link). Int4 is interesting, but only if quality stays within the thresholds in your eval harness.

3) Credits: the 12% uplift is promising. Procurement will need an explicit example of monthly token drawdown tied to batch vs sync usage to approve.

We can sign a pilot ASAP if we get: a short runbook for rollback, a lossless KV cache plan, and the dataset/eval metric you'll use to guard quality.

—Olivia
VP Product, Parcelly

---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Parcelly asks — draft ops and metrics

Looping here to draft the initial ops items for the kickoff. I'll put these in the shared doc: matter-of-fact runbook stubs, rollback steps, and the KV cache TTL/consistency model. Key points:
- For /generate-chat we recommend a 20ms batching window for burst consolidation + a 30-token prefix cache for frequent system prompts. That preserves p95 while capturing batching savings.
- For embeddings and rerank, batch windows of 250–500ms are acceptable; use async queues and shard by model-variant to keep latency predictable.
- Quantization plan: we run int8 on a snapshot in a canary pool (1 node) and measure Rouge/BLEU-style similarity and the eval harness score you provide. Int4 only if delta < 1.5% on your primary quality metric.

I'll attach a one-pager for procurement that maps token categories -> credit drawdown examples.

—Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@parcelly.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: SOW + credit schedule (updated)

Hi Olivia —

Attached is a redline of the SOW with an explicit credit drawdown schedule (monthly examples) and the DocuSign envelope linked below. Summary of the commercial changes:
- Month 1: 12% credit uplift applied as a pre-paid credit (applies to token usage up to agreed commit band).
- Months 2–6: baseline commit with 6% monthly rebate applied retrospectively on overages that fall inside the pilot band.
- Optional extension: if you commit to a 12-month annualized commit before pilot close, we can increase the uplift to 18% and lock pricing for 12 months.

Procurement asks we anticipate and prepared language for: IP/data retention, KMS integration, and an ops SLA for benchmark regressions.

Link: https://app.docusign.com/envelopes/0A12BC34D5

Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW_Parcelly_draft.docx]

---

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@parcelly.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit: request for concession + batching/quantization ops plan (Parcelly)

Thanks team —

This looks reasonable. Procurement has one final ask: can you show a worked example where caching reduces token usage for /generate-chat by 18% (we've measured a lot of shared system prompts). If you can include that worked example in the DocuSign packet and confirm the pilot kickoffs next Monday, we will route the DocuSign and share the model snapshot link (S3 share) same day.

Assuming that, Olivia
VP Product, Parcelly
